results.name: Basilique Saint-Sernin
results.why_it_is_special: Built between 1070 and 1300, it is the largest Romanesque church in Europe. Its 115-metre length, five naves, 64-metre transept, and more than 400 sculpted capitals make it an architectural masterpiece and a key stop on the Santiago de Compostela pilgrimage route.

results.name: Couvent des Jacobins
results.why_it_is_special: A jewel of Southern Gothic architecture built in the 13th–14th centuries. Its double nave culminates in the famous "Palmier des Jacobins" — a spectacular stone column whose 22 ribs fan out across the ceiling. The convent houses the relics of Saint Thomas Aquinas and hosts concerts and exhibitions in its cloister and refectory.

results.name: Musée des Augustins
results.why_it_is_special: Toulouse's fine-arts museum, housed in a 14th-century Gothic Augustinian convent. One of the oldest museums in France (founded 1793), it holds a unique collection of Romanesque and Gothic sculpture alongside paintings from the Middle Ages to the 20th century, including works by Rubens, Delacroix, and Corot.

results.name: Hôtel d'Assézat / Fondation Bemberg
results.why_it_is_special: One of Toulouse's finest Renaissance hôtels particuliers, built in the 16th century for pastel-trade merchant Pierre II d'Assézat. It now houses the Fondation Bemberg, a major private art collection spanning five centuries — from Renaissance masters (Titian, Veronese) to French Impressionists and Post-Impressionists (Bonnard, Canaletto).

results.name: Cité de l'Espace
results.why_it_is_special: A space-themed science centre featuring full-scale replicas of the Ariane 5 rocket, the Mir space station, and Soyuz modules, plus a planetarium and interactive exhibits including a mission-control mock-up. It reflects Toulouse's role as the capital of European aerospace and is the top-rated science museum in the city.
